method: Alternating previous/current clean source heads in the same checkout, serial fresh source-mode Desktop runs. Same CPU observer and unchanged budgets. Physical latencies include this observer; compare runs within this series. Native timing covers only the isolated-character interval, not the burst.

supervisor.note: Outer watchdog includes image packaging and is no larger than the canonical budget.

profile.method: SIGUSR1 before first send_text; SIGUSR2 at first subsequent complete-offer observation. Interval starts and stops on existing owner boundaries. Signal delivery can add idle boundaries; native counters freeze at stop. Physical trace includes this observer and is a paired diagnostic, not an unprofiled benchmark.

helper.method: Identical captured 150-control banks. Native execution, alternating order each repetition, six repetitions per source including the first. Each real helper call retains its 3,000,000-step bound; no other test runs concurrently. Host execute interval excludes fixture allocation and assertion work.

pixel_comparison.note: All three repetitions of each source head have identical initial, isolated-character, and final pixels. Between source heads, differences occupy only the File Explorer size columns for source-17.src and source-18.src: 119K becomes 120K as the measured production sources grew. Pad and Daybook pixels are identical. No pixels are masked in the reported counts.

limitations: Three pairs on a shared host are a diagnostic comparison, not a confidence interval or a fluidity qualification. Same hardware does not fix CPU frequency, migration, contention or cache state.
Thread CPU excludes descheduled time but does not normalize CPU throughput. CPU timing variation is observed; frequency, contention and cache effects were not individually measured.
The first-character interval includes native profiling and a small phase observer in all six runs. These timings should not be substituted for previous unprofiled latency measurements.
Signal delivery and owner-boundary start/stop add variable idle work to total step counts. Stable functional phases provide the stronger work comparison.
The burst runs with native profiling restored to disabled. Its frame grouping and input backpressure vary with timing; intended-due and actual-dispatch latencies are both retained.
No production code, execution limit, ABI, scheduler, source mode, input authority or presentation acknowledgement changed during this investigation. Existing full Desktop acceptance was not rerun.
